text: Why does GSST (Ge2Sb2Se4Te1) enable longer cascaded synapse chains than canonical GST (Ge2Sb2Te5)?
choices: GSST is engineered to be low-loss in BOTH amorphous and crystalline states while keeping a large index contrast, so per-cell insertion loss stays low; GST's crystalline state is strongly absorbing
GSST crystallizes faster, so signals spend less time in the lossy state
GSST stores more bits per cell, so fewer cells are needed
GSST is amplitude-modulating while GST is phase-modulating, giving GSST lower loss
explanation: GSST is low-loss in both states with a large index contrast, so cascaded cells accumulate little insertion loss, whereas GST's crystalline phase is strongly absorbing and limits chain length. Choice 3 reverses the modulation roles (GSST is phase-dominated, GST amplitude/absorptive); switching speed (1) and bit-depth (2) are not the cascadability mechanism.
